chunks: My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with them) narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abi Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) had children from Khadijah: Al-Qasim and Al-Tahir (who was also called Abdullah), Umm Kulthum, Ruqayyah, Zaynab, and Fatimah. Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) married Fatimah (peace be upon her). Abu al-As ibn al-Rabi', who was a man from Banu Umayyah, married Zaynab. Uthman ibn Affan married Umm Kulthum, but she died before he consummated the marriage with her. When they marched to Badr, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) married Ruqayyah to him. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) also had a son named Ibrahim from Maria al-Qibtiyya, who is also called Umm Ibrahim and Umm Walad.

key_terms.أَبُو الْعَاصِ: Abu al-As ibn al-Rabi', husband of Zaynab
key_terms.أُمُّ كُلْثُوم: Umm Kulthum, daughter of the Prophet
key_terms.خَدِيجَة: Khadijah, the first wife of the Prophet
key_terms.عُثْمَانُ بْنُ عَفَّان: Uthman ibn Affan, husband of Umm Kulthum
key_terms.مَارِيَة الْقِبْطِيَّة: Maria al-Qibtiyya, concubine of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: Who were the children of Prophet Muhammad from Khadijah and how were his daughters married?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* meticulously enumerates the Prophet’s seven children, distinguishing between those born to Khadijah and Maria al-Qtiyya, while clarifying the marital status of his daughters, such as Uthman’s marriage to Umm Kulthum after her sister Rqiyah’s death. It highlights the lineage of the Ahl al-Bayt through Fatimah and Ali, and Ibrahim, providing essential genealogical context for Shia claims regarding the Prophet’s pure progeny. The text serves as a primary source for understanding the domestic structure of the Prophet’s household and the early alliances formed through these marriages.
